scope: literal tokens in first-party Apollo-main C and header files, after Nema table relocation and I2C/UART duplicate-tail removal
method: C lexical scan skips block and line comments plus character and string literals, then recognizes hexadecimal integer tokens in [0x20000000,0x20400000). This is token triage, not pointer-use proof. The one-off scanner is under build/g2-apollo-ram-literal-audit-20261111/audit.py.
limits: Address-looking integers include packed protobuf descriptors, encoded UI values, bit masks, and symbolic stock offsets. The 212 remaining tokens require semantic classification before any is called a dangling pointer.
This scan covers only first-party g2/src/apollo-main .c and .h files; it does not inspect generated objects, upstream dependencies, computed addresses, or binary data outside C tokens.
